facts.value: Resident employee, 2026: (1) Nonstatutory option (NSO): the spread at exercise (FMV - price) is wages - a taxable fringe benefit subject to the supplemental-wage rules (22% optional flat or aggregate; 37% on supplemental wages above 1,000,000), FICA and FUTA wages, timed at the actual exercise (transfer) date; W-2 boxes 1, 3 (to the SS base), 5 and box 12 code V. (2) ISO and ESPP options: no FICA or FUTA at grant, exercise or disposition; no FIT withholding required on a disqualifying disposition or on the ESPP discount at a qualifying disposition, but the ordinary income is W-2 box 1 wages. (3) Restricted stock (actual shares subject to forfeiture): FMV minus amount paid is wages when substantially vested (or at transfer with an 83(b) election). (4) RSU (legally binding right to receive shares in a future year): FICA and FUTA wages at the later of service performance and vesting (special timing rule, 26 CFR 31.3121(v)(2)-1 / 31.3306(r)(2)-1); FIT withholding when the shares are delivered (settlement) as supplemental wages. (5) 83(i) election (private company): FIT deferred up to 5 years and withheld at 37% when included; FICA/FUTA not deferred; W-2 codes GG/HH.
facts.note: Rows: Pub. 15-B options and 83(i) (US-FEDQ1-001), Pub. 15 sec. 7 (US-FEDQ1-002), Pub. 525 (US-FEDQ1-003), 26 CFR 31.3121(v)(2)-1 (US-FEDQ1-004), 31.3306(r)(2)-1 (US-FEDQ1-005). Confidence medium only for the RSU limb: no IRS publication names RSUs in the FIT timing rule; it follows from settlement in shares (Pub. 15-B 83(i) paragraph) and the NQDC definition in 31.3121(v)(2)-1(b)(4)(iii). LEVEL: withholding.

facts.value: Nonresident alien employee, 2026: taxable fringe benefits are wages subject to graduated FIT withholding. Added to regular wages for the payroll period, they are withheld with the Pub. 15-T NRA add-on; withheld separately at the 22% optional flat supplemental rate (37% above 1,000,000), no add-on applies. Noncash fringes may be treated as paid per pay period, quarter, half-year or year (at least annually). FICA and FUTA apply as for residents unless the employee is an F-1/J-1/M-1/Q nonimmigrant. Group-term life cost over 50,000: FICA wages, no FIT withholding and no FUTA required, W-2 boxes 1, 3, 5 and box 12 code C. Only U.S.-source fringes are wages for withholding: housing, education, local transportation (main job location), tax reimbursement (taxing jurisdiction), hazardous duty and moving (new main job location) are sourced geographically, other fringes on a time basis. Reported on Form W-2 (Form 1042-S only for treaty-exempt wages on Form 8233).

facts.value: Pub. 15-T 2026 Worksheet 1A annualises the payroll-period wages by the number of pay periods in Table 3 (weekly 52, biweekly 26); Pub. 15 (2026) section 8: "When you have a regular payroll period, withhold income tax for that time period even if your employee doesn't work the full period"; neither copy contains a provision for a 27th biweekly or 53rd weekly payday (text search of both copies, 2026-11-03). Our reading: the extra payday is withheld as one more ordinary period. FICA wages are taken into account when actually or constructively paid (26 CFR 31.3121(v)(2)-1(a)(1)); FUTA counts remuneration paid in the calendar year up to the $7,000 base (IRC 3306(b)(1))
facts.note: Negative finding: full text of Pub. 15-T (2026) and Pub. 15 (2026) searched for 53/27-period provisions; none. FICA/FUTA paid-basis: Pub. 15 sec. 7/9 and 31.3121(v)(2)-1(a)(1) (US-FEDQ1-004). LEVEL: withholding.
facts._figure_located: 2026-11-03 agent 2 (precheck-next): word 'FICA' found in US-FED-015 00-official-sources/spec-sources/FED/eCFR_26CFR31.6011a-1_api_2026-11-03.xml p1: "ributions Act"
facts._value_before_r1: No IRS rule adjusts withholding for a 27th biweekly or 53rd weekly payday: Pub. 15-T Worksheet 1A annualises each payment with the Table 3 count for the payroll period (weekly 52, biweekly 26), and Pub. 15 sec. 8 requires withholding for the regular payroll period, so the extra payday is withheld as one more ordinary period. FICA and FUTA: wages are counted when paid, against the 2026 annual bases for wages paid in 2026.
facts._context_confirmed_r1: 2026-11-03 agent 2 (WTC fix R1): Pub. 15 copy (US-FEDS5-003) section 8 quoted in the value; Pub. 15-T copy (US-FEDQ1-007) Worksheet 1A: "Table 3 Semiannually Quarterly Monthly Semimonthly Biweekly Weekly Daily 2 4 12 24 26 52 260"; 31.3121(v)(2)-1 copy: "at the time the remuneration is actually or constructively paid"; US-MULTIS5-009 copy (IRC 3306(b)(1)): "$7,000 with respect to employment has been paid to an individual by an employer during any calendar year". The absence of a 27th/53rd provision is a text-search negative only. Also-id US-FED-015 (6011(a)-1) replaced.
